name: Recognise situations that use integers
description: Student can recognise everyday and financial situations that use negative integers.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says a temperature of minus 3 degrees and a debt of $5 use negative integers.
commonError: Student treats every number as positive, not recognising negatives in context.
checkpointTask: Name situations (temperature, money owed, floors below ground). Ask the student which use integers.

name: Locate an integer on a number line
description: Student can locate a positive or negative integer on a number line.
exampleOfSuccess: The student marks minus 4 to the left of zero.
commonError: Student places negatives to the right of zero, or in the wrong order.
checkpointTask: Give a number line through zero. Ask the student to mark several integers.

name: Order integers
description: Student can order a set of integers including negatives.
exampleOfSuccess: The student orders minus 5, minus 2, 0, 3 from least to greatest.
commonError: Student orders negatives as if larger ones are greater, putting minus 5 above minus 2.
checkpointTask: Give a set of integers. Ask the student to order them from least to greatest.

name: Use integers in a financial context
description: Student can use integers to represent amounts in a financial context.
exampleOfSuccess: The student writes a $20 debt as minus 20 and a $30 credit as plus 30.
commonError: Student writes both as positive, losing the direction.
checkpointTask: Pose financial situations. Ask the student to represent each with an integer.

name: Plot integers as coordinates
description: Student can plot points with integer coordinates on the Cartesian plane.
exampleOfSuccess: The student plots (minus 2, 3) in the correct quadrant.
commonError: Student ignores the sign and plots in the wrong quadrant.
checkpointTask: Give integer coordinates. Ask the student to plot each on the Cartesian plane.

name: Identify prime and composite numbers
description: Student can identify whether a number is prime or composite.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 7 is prime and 12 is composite.
commonError: Student calls 1 prime, or labels a number by appearance rather than its factors.
checkpointTask: Give numbers. Ask the student to classify each as prime or composite.

name: Explain why a number is prime or composite
description: Student can explain a classification using factors.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 13 is prime because its only factors are 1 and 13.
commonError: Student gives a classification with no reference to factors.
checkpointTask: Give numbers. Ask the student to classify each and explain why.

name: Identify square numbers
description: Student can identify square numbers and explain why.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 16 is a square number because 4 x 4 = 16.
commonError: Student confuses square numbers with even numbers or doubles.
checkpointTask: Give numbers. Ask the student which are square and why.

name: Express a composite number as a product of factors
description: Student can express a composite number as a product of its prime factors.
exampleOfSuccess: The student writes 24 as 2 x 2 x 2 x 3.
commonError: Student writes a product that does not equal the number, or stops before all factors are prime.
checkpointTask: Give composite numbers. Ask the student to express each as a product of factors.

name: Use number properties to simplify a calculation
description: Student can use prime, composite or square properties to simplify a calculation.
exampleOfSuccess: The student uses factors to simplify a multiplication.
commonError: Student does not use the properties to find an easier route.
checkpointTask: Pose calculations. Ask the student to use number properties to simplify each.

name: Find equivalent fractions to compare
description: Student can find equivalent fractions to compare two fractions.
exampleOfSuccess: To compare 2/3 and 3/4, the student rewrites both as twelfths.
commonError: Student compares numerators or denominators directly.
checkpointTask: Give pairs of fractions. Ask the student to find equivalents to compare them.

name: Compare and order common fractions
description: Student can compare and order common fractions including halves, thirds and quarters.
exampleOfSuccess: The student orders 1/2, 2/3, 3/4 correctly.
commonError: Student orders by numerator or denominator alone.
checkpointTask: Give several fractions. Ask the student to order them.

name: Represent fractions on the same number line
description: Student can place several fractions on the same number line.
exampleOfSuccess: The student places 1/2, 2/3 and 3/4 in the right positions on one line.
commonError: Student uses different scales for different fractions on the same line.
checkpointTask: Give a number line. Ask the student to place several fractions on it.

name: Justify the order of fractions
description: Student can justify the order of a set of fractions.
exampleOfSuccess: The student explains 2/3 is greater than 1/2 because 4/6 is more than 3/6.
commonError: Student orders correctly but cannot justify it.
checkpointTask: After ordering fractions, ask the student to justify the order.

name: Add decimals using place value
description: Student can add decimals by lining up place value.
exampleOfSuccess: For 3.45 plus 2.7, the student aligns the points and finds 6.15.
commonError: Student lines up the digits from the right instead of by place value.
checkpointTask: Pose decimal additions. Ask the student to solve using place value.

name: Subtract decimals using place value
description: Student can subtract decimals by lining up place value.
exampleOfSuccess: For 6.3 minus 2.45, the student aligns the points and finds 3.85.
commonError: Student misaligns the place values, or mishandles the empty place.
checkpointTask: Pose decimal subtractions. Ask the student to solve using place value.

name: Work with decimal measurements
description: Student can add or subtract linear measurements expressed as decimals.
exampleOfSuccess: The student adds 1.25 m and 0.8 m to get 2.05 m.
commonError: Student ignores the units or misaligns the decimals.
checkpointTask: Pose measurement problems with decimals. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Estimate to check a decimal calculation
description: Student can use estimation and rounding to check a decimal calculation.
exampleOfSuccess: For 3.45 plus 2.7, the student estimates about 6 and sees 6.15 is reasonable.
commonError: Student accepts an unreasonable answer without checking.
checkpointTask: Give answered decimal calculations. Ask the student to estimate and judge each.

name: Find a common denominator
description: Student can find a common denominator for two fractions with related denominators.
exampleOfSuccess: For 1/2 and 1/3, the student finds sixths.
commonError: Student multiplies the denominators without simplifying, or cannot find a common one.
checkpointTask: Give pairs of fractions. Ask the student to find a common denominator.

name: Add fractions with related denominators
description: Student can add fractions with related denominators using equivalence.
exampleOfSuccess: For 1/2 plus 1/3, the student finds 5/6.
commonError: Student adds numerators and denominators directly.
checkpointTask: Pose related-denominator additions. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Subtract fractions with related denominators
description: Student can subtract fractions with related denominators.
exampleOfSuccess: For 3/4 minus 1/3, the student finds 5/12.
commonError: Student subtracts without making the denominators the same.
checkpointTask: Pose related-denominator subtractions. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Solve a fraction problem in context
description: Student can solve a practical problem involving adding or subtracting fractions.
exampleOfSuccess: For a recipe needing 2/3 and 1/4 cups, the student finds 11/12 of a cup.
commonError: Student adds the numbers without using equivalent fractions.
checkpointTask: Pose practical fraction problems. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Multiply a decimal by a power of 10
description: Student can multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1000.
exampleOfSuccess: For 3.4 x 100, the student gives 340.
commonError: Student adds zeros instead of shifting the place value.
checkpointTask: Pose decimal multiplications by powers of 10. Ask the student to solve.

name: Divide a decimal by a power of 10
description: Student can divide a decimal by 10, 100 or 1000.
exampleOfSuccess: For 56 divided by 100, the student gives 0.56.
commonError: Student removes digits instead of shifting the place value.
checkpointTask: Pose decimal divisions by powers of 10. Ask the student to solve.

name: Explain the place value effect
description: Student can explain the effect of multiplying or dividing a decimal by a power of 10.
exampleOfSuccess: The student explains the digits shift one place left when multiplying by 10.
commonError: Student states the answer but cannot explain the place value shift.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to explain what happens to the digits when multiplying or dividing by 10.

name: Check the result with estimation
description: Student can use estimation to check a decimal multiplication or division.
exampleOfSuccess: For 3.4 x 100, the student estimates about 340 and confirms it.
commonError: Student does not check, or cannot estimate to compare.
checkpointTask: Give answered decimal calculations. Ask the student to estimate and judge each.

name: Find a fraction of a quantity
description: Student can find a familiar fraction of a quantity.
exampleOfSuccess: The student finds 1/3 of 24 by dividing by 3 to get 8.
commonError: Student multiplies by the denominator instead of dividing.
checkpointTask: Pose 'fraction of a quantity' problems. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Find a percentage of a quantity
description: Student can find a familiar percentage of a quantity.
exampleOfSuccess: The student finds 25% of 80 as 20.
commonError: Student treats the percentage as the answer, or uses the wrong operation.
checkpointTask: Pose 'percentage of a quantity' problems. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Find a decimal of a quantity
description: Student can find a decimal fraction of a quantity.
exampleOfSuccess: The student finds 0.5 of 60 as 30.
commonError: Student multiplies by the wrong place value.
checkpointTask: Pose 'decimal of a quantity' problems. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Calculate a percentage discount
description: Student can calculate a percentage discount on a price.
exampleOfSuccess: For 20% off $50, the student finds the discount is $10 and the price is $40.
commonError: Student finds the discount but forgets to subtract it, or finds the wrong percentage.
checkpointTask: Pose discount problems. Ask the student to find the discount and the final price.

name: Estimate using familiar fractions and percentages
description: Student can use familiar fractions, decimals and percentages to estimate.
exampleOfSuccess: The student estimates 48% of 200 as about half, so about 100.
commonError: Student tries to calculate exactly rather than estimating.
checkpointTask: Pose problems. Ask the student to estimate using familiar benchmarks.

name: Choose an estimation strategy
description: Student can choose an appropriate estimation strategy for a problem.
exampleOfSuccess: For a discount, the student rounds the price to estimate the saving.
commonError: Student uses a strategy that does not suit the problem.
checkpointTask: Pose problems. Ask the student which estimation strategy each needs.

name: Estimate in a financial context
description: Student can estimate a solution in a financial context.
exampleOfSuccess: The student estimates a shopping total to about $30 to check affordability.
commonError: Student calculates exactly when an estimate would do, or estimates poorly.
checkpointTask: Pose financial problems. Ask the student to estimate each.

name: Recognise the effect of rounding
description: Student can recognise how rounding affects a calculation.
exampleOfSuccess: The student notices rounding up both numbers gives an overestimate.
commonError: Student does not consider the direction of the rounding error.
checkpointTask: Pose rounded calculations. Ask the student how the rounding affects the result.

name: Choose operations for a percentage problem
description: Student can choose efficient operations for a practical percentage or rational number problem.
exampleOfSuccess: For a discount problem, the student chooses to find the percentage then subtract.
commonError: Student chooses operations that do not fit the situation.
checkpointTask: Pose practical problems. Ask the student which operations each needs.

name: Model a practical percentage problem
description: Student can model and solve a practical problem involving percentages.
exampleOfSuccess: The student models a sale price using a percentage discount.
commonError: Student applies the percentage to the wrong amount.
checkpointTask: Pose percentage problems. Ask the student to model and solve each.

name: Model a budget
description: Student can model a practical financial problem such as a budget involving rational numbers.
exampleOfSuccess: The student builds a budget with costs, income and a balance.
commonError: Student leaves out an amount or does not reach a balance.
checkpointTask: Pose a budgeting problem. Ask the student to model and solve it.

name: Interpret and justify the solution
description: Student can interpret and communicate the solution, justifying the choices made.
exampleOfSuccess: The student explains the budget balances and why their method works.
commonError: Student gives an answer without justifying the method or relating it to the context.
checkpointTask: After a problem, ask the student to interpret the answer and justify their method.
